sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: Arrays are the simplest and most ubiquitous data structure. Most coding interview problems use arrays or strings as input. The two-pointer and sliding window patterns reduce O(n²) brute-force solutions to O(n) — knowing these patterns is the single biggest upgrade you can make to your coding interview performance.

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
- **Two Pointers**: Two indices moving toward each other (or away from each other) to avoid a nested loop. Use when the array is sorted or when looking for a pair/triplet.
- **Sliding Window**: A window of variable or fixed size that slides over the array. Use when the problem asks for 'maximum/minimum/longest subarray/substring satisfying a condition'.
- **Prefix Sum**: Pre-compute cumulative sums so any range sum query is O(1) instead of O(n). Use when the problem involves range sums or subarray sum conditions.
- **Frequency Map**: Use a HashMap<Character/Integer, Integer> to count occurrences. Use for anagram, first-unique, and top-K problems.
- **String immutability**: Always use StringBuilder for building strings in loops; String concatenation with + in a loop is O(n²).

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
- **array-basics**: Arrays.sort() is O(n log n); Arrays.copyOf() is O(n); array default values are 0/false/null.
- **two-pointers**: Valid Palindrome (inward pointers), Two Sum in sorted array (inward), Container With Most Water.
- **sliding-window**: Longest substring without repeating chars (variable window with Set); Max sum subarray of size k (fixed window).
- **prefix-sum**: Build prefix[i] = prefix[i-1] + arr[i]; range sum [l,r] = prefix[r] - prefix[l-1].
- **anagram-palindrome**: Anagram → sort both strings or compare frequency maps; Palindrome → two pointers from ends.
- **frequency-map**: Build map, then scan — works for first unique char (LinkedHashMap) and top-K frequent.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- *"How would you solve two-sum in O(n)?"* — Use a HashMap: store complement as key, return when found.
- *"What is the sliding window technique?"* — Maintain a window [left, right] that expands right and contracts left based on a condition.
- *"Find the longest substring without repeating characters."* — Sliding window with a HashSet; move left pointer when a duplicate is found.
- *"How do you check if two strings are anagrams?"* — Compare sorted versions or compare frequency arrays/maps.
- *"What is the time complexity of your solution?"* — Always state O(n) or O(n log n) with justification.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"For this problem I recognize the [two-pointer / sliding window / prefix sum] pattern because [condition], so my approach is [O(n) description], and the time complexity is O(n) with O(1) or O(n) space."*
